Guideline: Build on the vendored Bootstrap 5 PUMA theme
Description: PUMA ships a pinned, vendored Bootstrap 5 so pages render with zero build step (no npm, no bundler).
Do: Use PUMA's bundled Bootstrap grid, utilities and components as the layout baseline
Don't: Add a separate Bootstrap build pipeline or hotlink a CDN copy
Code Good: Use PUMA's bundled .container/.row/.col + utility classes directly in .phtml
Code Bad: Adding webpack/vite just to compile the Bootstrap that Tiger already vendors

Guideline: Theme a site by adding a skin, not by forking CSS
Description: A skin is a small --bs-* CSS-variable overlay in themes/puma/assets/skins/; skins are auto-discovered and selected per site.
Do: Create a new skin file that only overrides --bs-* custom properties
Don't: Copy the whole stylesheet to change a few colors
Code Bad: Editing core Bootstrap CSS or hardcoding hex values in views

Guideline: Express color and mode via CSS variables
Description: Light/dark and brand color live in the skin's --bs-* variables so components recolor without markup changes.
Do: Reference semantic Bootstrap variables (--bs-primary, --bs-body-bg) in custom CSS
Don't: Hardcode brand hex codes inside component styles

Description: Views are server-rendered PHP templates; keep branching thin and push data assembly into services/controllers.
Do: Render markup from data the controller already prepared
Don't: Query the database or build business logic inside a .phtml
Code Good: foreach ($this->items as $item) { ... } over a prepared collection
Code Bad: Running DB queries or service calls from inside the view

Guideline: No inline script or style in views
Description: FUNDAMENTAL rule: .phtml must not contain inline script or style (CMS-authored content is the only exception).
Do: Put JS in an asset file and CSS in the skin
Don't: Drop a script or style block into a view template
Code Bad: An inline script tag calling initChart() inside the .phtml

Description: Static theme assets live under /_theme and are resolved with the asset() helper so paths survive core updates.
Do: Emit asset URLs with asset('js/app.js') so they resolve under /_theme
Don't: Hardcode /application/... or absolute filesystem paths in markup

Guideline: Load dynamic data from the /api message endpoint
Description: Client-side widgets fetch structured data from the internal /api service (role-filtered) rather than embedding data in HTML.
Do: Fetch JSON from /api and render it into a placeholder element
Don't: Inline large JSON blobs or PHP-echoed data into the DOM
Code Bad: Echoing a big json_encode($rows) into a data attribute

Guideline: Build forms with Tiger_Form and array config
Description: Forms are Zend_Form subclasses configured with array element definitions; they render, validate and repopulate consistently.
Do: Declare elements in an array config and let Tiger_Form render and validate
Don't: Hand-write form markup with manual validation in the view
Code Bad: A raw input element with ad-hoc JS validation and no server check

Guideline: Validate in the service, then run the transaction
Description: Service methods validate input first and only then perform the write inside a transaction (validate then transaction).
Do: Validate all inputs before opening the DB transaction
Code Bad: Writing rows first and validating afterward

Guideline: Treat complex widgets as opaque GrapesJS components
Description: Complex theme widgets are components that GENERATE html; GrapesJS saves that markup verbatim unless the user edits it (never round-trip complex markup).
Do: Generate the widget HTML once and let the builder store it verbatim
Don't: Re-parse and re-serialize rich widget markup on every save
Code Good: Register a component that outputs finished HTML (marquee is the reference)
Code Bad: Round-tripping nested widget markup through the editor on each save

Description: PUMA buttons use Bootstrap .btn classes so button variants, sizing and focus recolor via --bs-* skin tokens.
Don't: Style bespoke buttons with inline CSS
Code Bad: A button with inline background and color styles

Guideline: Give icon buttons an accessible label
Description: Icon-only buttons need an accessible name; the skin themes the button focus ring.
Do: Add aria-label to icon buttons and keep the .btn focus outline
Don't: Ship icon buttons with no label
Code Bad: An icon button with no label and no aria-label

Guideline: Drive menus from menus.ini via Tiger_Menu
Description: A theme ships configs/menus.ini as the base menu tier; Tiger_Menu renders it with a live fallback and explicit CMS import.
Do: Define navigation in menus.ini and render via the nav view seam
Don't: Hardcode nav link lists directly in a layout .phtml
Code Good: Ship configs/menus.ini and render $this->nav in the layout
Code Bad: Pasting a static list of links into every layout

Description: Everything is a labeled partial: reusable sections are named partials included by shortcode or the layout, editable in one place.
Do: Extract repeated sections into named partials and include them
Don't: Duplicate the same markup block across multiple views
Code Good: [partial name="cta"] or a partial() include in the layout
Code Bad: Copy-pasting the hero or footer HTML into each page

Guideline: Rely on semantic Bootstrap components for a11y
Description: PUMA's Bootstrap components carry sensible ARIA and keyboard behavior; prefer them over custom widgets.
Do: Use the framework modal/dropdown/nav components and keep their semantics
Don't: Rebuild interactive widgets from bare divs without roles or keyboard
Code Bad: Custom div menus with click-only handlers and no roles
